title: Function Calls
concept: Calling a function executes its code with the arguments you provide, then continues from where you called it.
why: Functions are useless if you never call them. Understanding how invocation works is essential to making functions do work.
tips: Arguments are evaluated BEFORE the function body runs
The number of arguments must match the number of parameters
Functions can be called from other functions, including themselves (recursion)
Calling a function is also called 'invoking' or 'applying' a function
common_mistakes: Forgetting the parentheses: `my_func` vs `my_func()` — only the second calls it
Wrong number of arguments: `add(5)` when it expects two
